subject: Runway Recast & Approval Ladder — ACMEHealth MAP evaluation timeline
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Hargreaves <tim.h@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Recasting the MAP runway — initial ask

Hi Tim,

Thanks again for the session yesterday. After reviewing the ACME evaluation schedule and your internal availability windows, we see a 10–14 business day drift on the integration validation step (item 4 on the MAP). That pushes expected go-live out and compresses the acceptance window.

To keep things transparent and avoid surprises near procurement/signoff, I propose a formal runway recast: move the evaluation completion target by two calendar weeks, then apply a two-tier approval ladder so we can unblock the integration tests earlier if ACME can greenlight limited acceptance criteria.

I've attached a suggested rebaseline (ACME_MAP_Rebaseline.xlsx) and a short risk log that documents the primary slippage drivers. Can you confirm: 1) whether procurement needs a new PO timeline to match the recast; 2) whether Legal (cc Allison) will require revised contractual milestones?

If useful, I can run a 20-minute alignment call with procurement and your integration lead — propose Thursday morning.

Thanks,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134
Redwood Inference

Attachment: ACME_MAP_Rebaseline.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: runway_risk_log_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Tim Hargreaves <tim.h@acmehealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, Allison Tan <allison.t@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2028-11-19T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recasting the MAP runway — initial ask

Grace —

Appreciate the proactive note and the files. We do have a blocker on our side: the integration team's primary SME is out the week of Nov 20 and their earliest lift is Nov 29. That aligns with your two-week suggestion, but procurement will want the PO and milestone dates to reflect any downstream changes.

Allison — can Legal confirm if shifting milestone-based payments by 14 days requires an amendment or if we can accept an updated SOW addendum? Procurement — I'll need a quick confirmation on whether a PO amendment is required; otherwise we risk invoice timing mismatch.

Tim

--
Tim Hargreaves
Director of Digital Delivery, ACMEHealth
tim.h@acmehealth.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Hargreaves <tim.h@acmehealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-20T08:25:00-08:00
Subject: Approval ladder and contingency suggestions

Tim/Grace —

Saw the context — two quick operational items from my side:

- Approval ladder: propose a two-stage approval so ACME can sign off on Integration Validation as a gated limited-acceptance milestone (deliverable A) while final acceptance remains gated on end-to-end performance tests (deliverable B). That lets you start ramping internal training and integration earlier.

- Contingency: recommend a short-term dev-credit buffer (10k tokens equivalent) to be applied automatically should we need a one-week burst for retesting; this avoids reworking the invoice schedule for a small technical re-run.

If Legal requires an SOW addendum for the milestone split, we can prep language and a one-paragraph amendment to avoid lengthy redlines. Ben — curious if finance can approve a dev-credit buffer as a one-off?

Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Allison Tan <allison.t@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Tim Hargreaves <tim.h@acmehealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-11-20T13:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Approval ladder and contingency suggestions

Team —

We can accept a one-paragraph SOW addendum that splits the Integration Validation (deliverable A) and Final Acceptance (deliverable B), provided payment milestones are explicitly called out and the acceptance criteria for A are concrete. Please include the exact test cases and a sign-off owner for A.

Procurement, please confirm whether ACME needs a PO amendment for milestone date shifts. If yes, indicate the PO number and the preferred amendment workflow.

Allison

--
Allison Tan
Sr. Counsel, ACMEHealth
allison.t@acmehealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Hargreaves <tim.h@acmehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-23T15:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Runway recast & approval ladder — internal approval

Quick update from Finance: we can offer a dev-credit buffer up to the equivalent of $6,000 in test-run usage as a one-time concession for ACME without modifying invoicing terms (tied to deliverable A sign-off). That should cover a one-week burst if integration requires retests.

I'll draft the concession note (short paragraph) and share for Legal to attach as an addendum. Grace — please confirm you'd like Finance to proceed with the concession note and I'll run it through the standard approval queue (should be 24–48 hours).

Ben

--
Ben Carter
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
Attachment: concession_note_draft.docx (docx)
